title: Version Curation Inspector — compact cards and guided pin preview
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Engineers and product owners onboarding new model variants struggle to quickly decide which model version to pin for production. The current console list forces them to open multiple pages to view perf snapshots, token-cost estimates, and qualitative differences (e.g., hallucination/regression notes). This increases context switches and slows rollout decisions.

Goal: Design a compact 'Version Curation Inspector' — a right-side flyout that surfaces concise performance cards for candidate model versions, a guided pin preview flow, and safe publish controls for performance profiles. The experience should let users compare latency/cost/quality trade-offs, preview how a pin will affect traffic, and attach a performance profile with a single action.

Scope: UI patterns (compact cards, inline deltas, pin-preview modal), copy/labels, accessibility, and micro-interactions for publish confirmation. Engineering will implement data wiring (perf snapshots, cost model) separately. This ticket contains the design spec and handoff artifacts.

Out of scope: full rollout automation UX (canary knobs), detailed billing export views, deep evaluation editor (separate PRD).
acceptance_criteria: A right-side inspector opens from the model version list with a compact card for each version (max 6 visible; scrollable), each card showing version name, recent latency P95, median token cost estimate for the selected prompt set, and a one-line note for recent regressions or strengths.
Users can multi-select up to 3 versions for side-by-side comparison; comparison view shows normalized deltas and color-coded flags for regressions (red), neutral (amber), or improvements (green).

Pin preview flow lets users choose pin target (production/staging), preview expected latency and monthly cost delta, set a roll-out window, and attach a published performance profile before finalizing. Preview uses current traffic profile for estimates.

Publish button triggers a two-step confirmation (publish profile + pin) with an inline checklist: performance profile matches baseline tests, smoke evals green, and required approvers present. Missing items disable publish and surface required actions.
All UI elements meet AA contrast and keyboard navigation; inspector is responsive down to 960px width and collapses to modal on narrow screens.
Design tokens and component specs provided in Figma and a short accessibility notes doc in Drive for engineering handoff.
design_notes: Card density: prefer compact cards with 2–3 lines of text to reduce vertical scanning. Use an overline for model family and bold version label.
Show performance deltas as small inline sparklines + numeric delta (e.g., +18ms) with tooltip that explains the measurement window (last 7 days, 95th percentile).
Cost estimate: show 'expected extra tokens / month' as a secondary metric and a tooltip linking to the cost model doc. Avoid showing raw dollars to reduce noise for early experiments.

Pin preview trade-off: Offer an escape hatch to 'simulate pin for 24h' which creates a temporary canary to surface regressions; if engineering cannot support simulation, show a clear 'simulation unavailable' state and default to conservative estimates.

Profile publishing: single-click publish should create an immutable profile snapshot linked to the version and show a permalink for audits. If policy requires approvals, disable publish and show approver list.
tasks: Create compact card component in Figma with variants for neutral/improvement/regression states
Design multi-select comparison strip and delta visualization
Write copy for pin preview modal and two-step publish confirmation
Document keyboard flows and accessibility notes
Handoff: export tokens, spacing, and states; add implementation checklist for ENG
Follow up with PM/Eng sync to finalize required telemetry fields for cost/latency estimates
risks_and_tradeoffs: Showing cost in dollars can be misleading due to region/hardware variance; we opt to surface token-based delta by default and link to an expanded cost page.
Compact cards may hide nuance for edge-case experiments; we provide 'expand card' to reveal full perf snapshot if needed, avoiding clutter by default.
Publishing a profile as part of pin action reduces friction but increases blast radius; mitigate with an approval checklist and optional canary simulation.
implementation_notes: Backend needs endpoints: /versions/:id/perf_snapshot (last-7d), /simulate_pin (optional), /profiles (publish). Coordinate with ENG-4120 for payload shapes.
Telemetry: fire events for inspector_open, compare_selected, preview_pin, publish_profile, and attach_profile. Include model_version, actor_role, and selected_prompt_set in payloads.
Fallback: if perf data is missing, show 'insufficient data' badge and disable cost estimate; include a link to run an on-demand eval.
